c: Uxbridge properties range from tight downtown lots to sprawling rural acreages, and something eventually needs to come down on both. Live Junk Free tears it down and hauls it away, wherever the address sits. Along Brock Street and the town’s Victorian streets, it’s a fence, a deck or a small shed that’s finally past its life, demolished with the same care given to anything else on a heritage property. Through the hamlets of Goodwood, Zephyr, Leaskdale and Sandford, it’s above ground pool demolition, garage teardowns and larger shed removals on bigger rural lots. On the working farms across the concessions, it’s fencing, sheds and old structures that came with the land, cleared alongside whatever else needs to go. And for the township’s studio owners and craftspeople, it’s an old structure demolished to make way for workshop space instead. The 700+ five-star Google reviews behind Live Junk Free come from every one of those properties — a demolition crew that tore the structure down safely, set aside anything worth salvaging, and hauled the rest away the same visit, no matter how far down the concession the job was sitting.

blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Uxbridge — What to Know Before You Book

items.q: How much does demolition cost in Uxbridge?
a: Price depends on the structure — a fence section or trampoline is a small job; a full above ground pool, garage or concrete pad costs more given the size, material and crew time involved — with no township or distance premium anywhere. The exact figure is confirmed free at the walkthrough.

items.q: Do you charge extra for rural properties or long laneways?
a: Never. The same flat pricing applies at a Brock Street backyard and at the end of a concession laneway — no distance fee, no rural markup, no exceptions.

items.q: Can the good wood or materials from a demolished deck or shed be saved?
a: Often, yes — say so at the walkthrough. Boards, hardware and anything else worth keeping come out intact and set aside for your projects before the rest is hauled, sorted at no extra charge.

items.q: Do you handle fence demolition on larger rural properties?
a: Yes — long fence runs and multiple structures on farm properties are regular work for us, priced the same flat way as a single backyard fence section.

items.q: What's involved in concrete or flooring demolition?
a: The pad, walkway or patio gets broken up with equipment matched to its thickness and reinforcement, then hauled off in manageable pieces. The site is left level and cleared, ready for whatever’s next.

items.q: Can demolition happen the same day I call?
a: Often, yes. Trucks run Uxbridge daily, 6AM to 11PM, seven days a week, so a morning call frequently means an afternoon demolition — call +1 647 922 5865 for today’s real availability.

items.q: Do you cover the hamlets — Goodwood, Zephyr, Leaskdale, Sandford?
a: Every one, at the same flat pricing as downtown. Demolition on those concessions rides the same daily routes; no address waits longer or pays more.

items.q: What happens to the materials after demolition?
a: Metal components go to recyclers, salvageable wood or hardware sets aside where flagged, and the remainder disposed of responsibly. Nothing goes to landfill that has a better destination.
